raw.assessment: The incumbent supplies a reversible, preassembled organizer and a layout diagram, but its combined median time is 11 minutes (D2-O2), five customers reported partition discrepancies (D2-O3), and only seven of ten observed customers achieved their arrangement unaided (D2-O4). These observations do not establish whether discrepancies arose during picking or interpretation. Repeated three-compartment orders taking seven to nine minutes (D2-O6) limit an account that assembly is intrinsically too slow: batch composition or layout complexity may matter, but they are confounded. Width overlap among first- and second-attempt insertions (D2-O5) also weakens a simple width-only explanation without excluding slot or orientation effects. No proposed change is yet shown to meet all pilot targets.

openings.claim: Hypothesis: order-specific picking areas reduce part-selection interference during mixed-layout work.
openings.delta: Use removable picking mats made from spare board, with compartment-count and exterior-color positions, before the existing assembly and check steps.
openings.prediction: Within the same layout and worker, mats reduce selection/checking time and independently counted content discrepancies; insertion time changes little.
openings.probe: Counterbalance mat and shared-bin trials across both workers on repeated mixed-layout samples. Time each stage and independently compare contents with order slips. Reuse samples and mats; count setup time and require it to fit the fixed delivery schedule before adoption.
assumptions: Spare board can supply reusable mats within the initial budget.
Product geometry, capacity, color and partition counts stay as ordered.

openings.claim: Does the generic diagram leave customers unable to locate an otherwise correct short partition?
openings.delta: Distinguish diagram interpretation from actual missing or incompatible parts.
openings.prediction: If interpretation dominates, an order-specific diagram improves correct placement without assistance on independently verified complete kits; insertion difficulties may persist.
openings.probe: Randomly split the ten participants between the existing diagram and a same-size order-specific diagram. Use matched, verified sample kits; record placement, help requests and insertion retries separately. Treat results as exploratory. Price replacement diagrams before rollout, retaining the 0.40 recurring-cost ceiling.
assumptions: Diagram preparation fits the initial budget and delivery schedule.
Participants' prior exposure is balanced between groups.

raw.assessment: The observations do not separate incomplete picking, insertion difficulty and instruction ambiguity. Mixed batches may involve switching overhead or harder layouts; overlapping widths do not exclude other insertion causes. Both proposals are hypotheses. Fifteen samples and ten participants can discriminate mechanisms, but cannot establish the full 60-order success criteria.

openings.claim: Hypothesis: collecting and checking each order's complete component set in a dedicated reusable tray before insertion reduces omissions and repeated selection work.
openings.delta: Replace direct assembly from shared shape bins with an order-specific kit and count map; retain existing parts, selected layout and exterior color.
openings.prediction: At matched layout complexity, kits reduce selection interruptions and incorrect or missing components. Total assembly and packing time falls only if savings exceed the new checking work.
openings.probe: Use available samples in counterbalanced repeated assembly trials by both workers, comparing current picking with reusable spare-board trays. Include all three compartment counts and uncommon colors. Independently audit contents and time selection, insertion, checking and packing separately. Compare total times, including tray reset.
assumptions: Use existing slips for count maps and reusable trays without changing supplied components.
Proceed only within the 500 initial and 0.40 recurring caps and without delaying accepted orders.

openings.claim: A layout-specific instruction diagram may resolve short-partition confusion even when the supplied component set is correct.
openings.delta: Replace the generic three-layout diagram with the customer's ordered arrangement, explicitly showing both connection points of each short partition.
openings.prediction: With independently verified complete kits, the revised diagram reduces requests about short partitions and increases unaided correct arrangements within ten minutes.
openings.probe: Randomly assign five participants to each diagram using matched ordered layouts and verified kits. Record placement errors, questions and completion time; separately measure workshop diagram-selection time and cost. Treat results as directional evidence, not proof of 90% customer success.
assumptions: Replacement diagrams use the existing instruction medium within the same shared budget caps.
Parts remain dismantlable and the accepted arrangement, color, footprint, capacity and delivery date remain fixed.

openings.claim: Reusable order-specific picking mats/trays with count/color positions and pre-insertion checking may reduce interference and omissions.
openings.discriminator: Selection/checking errors and time fall within worker/layout; insertion changes little; added checking/reset may erase savings.
openings.fit: Preserves product constraints; budget and schedule conditional.
openings.probe: Counterbalance current picking against mats/trays using 15 reusable samples, both workers, mixed batches, all counts and uncommon colors. Independently audit contents; separately time selection, insertion, checking, packing, setup and reset.
openings.uncertainty: Switching and complexity are confounded; discrepancy reports may reflect interpretation.

openings.claim: Order-specific diagrams showing both short-partition connection points may resolve placement confusion.
openings.discriminator: Verified complete kits yield more unaided correct arrangements and fewer questions; insertion difficulty may persist.
openings.fit: Preserves product constraints; diagram preparation, selection and replacement costs conditional.
openings.probe: Randomize ten participants five per diagram; balance prior exposure and match layouts/verified kits. Record ten-minute completion, placement errors, help requests and insertion retries separately; measure workshop diagram time/cost.
openings.uncertainty: Exploratory evidence cannot establish 90% success; width overlap leaves slot/orientation causes unresolved.

post_distill.decision: Probe both hypotheses. Preserve 30x20 cm footprint, capacity, reversible partitions, accepted counts/colors and delivery date. Combined initial cost <=500 and recurring addition <=0.40/order. Neither establishes pilot targets: >=98% complete, median <=8 minutes, >=90% unaided across 60 units.
